basics.name: Lucas Horsman
basics.label: Robotics & Software Engineer • Computer Science Student
basics.summary: Computer Science student in the Department of Information and Computer Sciences at the University of Hawaii at Manoa (graduating Spring 2026). Specializing in robotics software, real-time control (GNC), sensor fusion, computer vision, and systems programming.

interests.name: Robotics Control, Autonomous Vehicles, Computer Vision, Real-Time Systems, Embedded Systems, Video Game Development, Music (KTUH DJ), Sci-Fi

work.position: Software Developer Intern — FOBOS Control System
responsibilities: Built a PySide6 GUI with Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture to control a set of robotic fiber positioners, integrating GigE Vision camera feeds and CAN bus communication.
Designed a homography-based calibration system mapping camera pixels to focal plane coordinates.
Diagnosed a VPN/GigE Vision protocol incompatibility blocking camera integration; designed and deployed a Raspberry Pi 5 hardware bridge to resolve it.

Built a real-time guidance, navigation, and control system (GNC) for a differential-drive robot using ROS2, NAV2, EKF sensor fusion, and LiDAR, enabling automated patrol routes and repeatable odometry testing.
Diagnosed and resolved intermittent low-level hardware faults in sensor and motor controller interfaces, isolating root causes across firmware and communication layers.
Deployed a Zenoh-based pub/sub architecture to route messages between desktop and robot over network links, addressing discovery limitations of default DDS transport across VPN-bridged networks.
Experimented with alternative methods of localization utilizing computer vision techniques and Time-of-Flight sensors.
Authored publication-ready technical documentation for the system.
Deployed and field-tested an autonomous ROS2 navigation system on a physical rover operating in an unstructured agricultural environment, using RTK localization for real-time path planning.
Led development of a ROS2 system for an autonomous tree-climbing robot, integrating MCUs, micro-ROS, and motor controllers under a central control package.
Built an image-stitching pipeline for overhead field data collection.

work.company: Autonomous RC Car State Estimation & Control
responsibilities: Built a simple controller for an Arduino based remote controlled car.
Designed a Kalman filter fusing IMU acceleration with dead-reckoning speed to localize a robot with no wheel encoders.
Built ESP32–Arduino communication pipeline with an HTTP/JSON API and GUI for path planning and live pose visualization, under 2KB RAM constraints.
Taught weekly programming fundamentals (languages, variables, control structures) to 3rd–8th grade students via original curriculum.
Adapted teaching style and pacing across a wide age range, balancing structured curriculum with public speaking and improvisation to keep varying skill levels engaged.
Provided direct technical assistance and hardware/software troubleshooting for computer lab users.
Maintained lab infrastructure, ensuring reliable workstation performance and network availability.
Developed the robot’s primary control system, autonomous control, and auxiliary functions through expert programming, driving efficient and effective performance of the club's robotic systems.
Demonstrated strong leadership skills by training the electronics team on electrical and pneumatic systems for the robot, enhancing the team's technical knowledge and abilities.
Created and implemented innovative solutions to complex problems, streamlining testing processes and contributing to the club's success.
Orchestrated all A/V needs for the theater, ensuring seamless and high-quality movie experiences for patrons.
Revitalized the theater's online presence by designing and regularly updating the theater's website, increasing visibility and sales.
Provided instruction to students on how to operate theater equipment such as projectors and headphones, enriching their knowledge and experience in audio-visual technologies.
